proposal.name: Run Python checks with application dependencies

plan.name: Run Python checks with application dependencies
plan.summary: Build and reuse an application image from project-root requirements.txt and its recursive local requirement and constraint files, using the existing digest-pinned Python base on linux/amd64, without rewriting application inputs or falling back after installation or evidence failure. This first slice accepts PyPI wheel requirements with names, versions, extras, markers and pip hashes only in UTF-8 files with an optional leading UTF-8 BOM and LF or CRLF line endings, rejects invalid UTF-8, every bare CR and every encoding declaration anywhere in root or referenced files before interpreting comments or continuations, rejects source distributions, URLs, VCS, editable or local packages, environment substitutions, index overrides and all non-CR/LF line separators recognized by Python splitlines before parsing comments or continuations, keys reuse on the full recipe and every referenced input, copies a dedicated inputs directory literally with every in-project directory a reference traverses (including empty directories canceled by '..'), and runs every build-side Python invocation with -I from a clean directory outside those inputs. Resolve one immutable Docker image ID for each selected application environment and use it for evidence reads, Python tests, conformance and larger-bound runs despite concurrent recipe-tag replacement, keep Nagini separate and the no-requirements standard-library path intact, and include canonical input hashes and resolved wheel names, versions, filenames and SHA-256 hashes in JSON and Markdown receipts and their fingerprints; cached images retain their actual resolution, while fresh builds of unpinned requirements may resolve differently. Preserve all earlier acceptance coverage and additionally run the evidence reader, ordinary and larger-bound launchers, and every external helper in their check scripts (including timeout) by trusted absolute paths outside the application dependency environment, leaving shell builtins and application Python intact; retain the regression with a wheel installing cat, sh and timeout, add the encoding-declaration exploit and coverage for every encoding rule and traversed directory, and require the merger to run the INVARIANT_PYTHON_DEPS_REAL=1 suite on the final pull request head and post its passing output before merge, and update SPEC.md and README to describe supported forms and encodings, preserved reference directories, build isolation, trusted gate commands, offline execution and fingerprints that agree only for the same effective environment. The merger must record the dependency-policy decision and cite it with the existing grounding decisions in changed SPEC bullets under D-0122; attaching this reusable environment evidence to component receipts remains later work because the base branch has component inventory and proof attribution but no component execution, while Python existing-code discovery and contract checks remain subsequent issues on #210.

tests.name: TestPythonDependencyRecipeCoversReferencedInputs
tests.says: The recipe covers the recursive requirement and constraint closure, is independent of checkout location and unrelated source, and accepts the documented wheel requirement syntax without changing input files.

tests.name: TestPythonDependenciesRejectUnaccountedInputs
tests.says: Unsupported requirement sources, escaping or symlinked paths, missing references and reference cycles fail before any dependency installation can run.

tests.name: TestPythonDependencyImagesBuildReuseAndRunOffline
tests.says: A dependency image is built once and reused with its recorded wheel provenance, referenced constraints invalidate it, and Python checks use it offline; INVARIANT_PYTHON_DEPS_REAL=1 additionally exercises the same fixture against real Docker and PyPI.

tests.name: TestPythonDependencyFailuresDoNotFallBack
tests.says: Installation failure or missing or malformed resolved artifact evidence prevents Python execution and produces an actionable error rather than a standard-library fallback.

tests.name: TestPythonGateRecordsAndReusesApplicationEnvironment
tests.says: The gate records the environment used by tests and conformance, reuses it one size larger, leaves Nagini's pinned verifier independent, and preserves projects without requirements.

tests.name: TestPythonReceiptIdentifiesResolvedDependencies
tests.says: The receipt shows the Python application base, recipe and resolved artifact evidence separately from Nagini.

tests.name: TestPythonFingerprintTracksResolvedDependencies
tests.says: Dependency evidence survives JSON receipts and changes the fingerprint when effective inputs, platform or resolved artifacts change.

tests.name: TestPythonDependenciesRejectHiddenPipOptions
tests.says: Every non-CR/LF separator recognized by Python splitlines is rejected in root and referenced inputs before Docker can run, including options hidden after a comment.

tests.name: TestPythonDependenciesPinImageAcrossTagReplacement
tests.says: Even when a concurrent build replaces the recipe tag between selection, evidence reads, tests and larger-bound checks, all reads and runs use one immutable image ID and the receipt describes that image.

tests.name: TestPythonDependencyRecipeIsolatesInputModules
tests.says: Build-side Python uses isolated mode and a clean working directory; with INVARIANT_PYTHON_DEPS_REAL=1 the generated recipe actually builds and runs offline despite referenced venv.py and pip.py files that fail if executed.

tests.name: TestPythonDependencyRecipeCopiesLiteralFilenames
tests.says: A dedicated inputs directory is copied literally; with INVARIANT_PYTHON_DEPS_REAL=1 the generated recipe installs the version required by distinct [a].txt and a.txt inputs, and evidence hashes the bytes pip actually read.

tests.name: TestPythonDependenciesKeepGateCommandsTrusted
tests.says: Dependency-installed cat, sh and timeout cannot replace the gate evidence reader or ordinary and larger-bound checks; the real-Docker layer executes the generated recipe, installs a hostile fixture wheel offline, and verifies unchanged receipt evidence and successful and failing application checks.

tests.name: TestPythonDependenciesAcceptUTF8Inputs
tests.says: Root and referenced requirement and constraint files accept UTF-8 with or without its leading BOM and LF or CRLF endings, preserve the exact staged bytes and input hashes, and reuse their environment; INVARIANT_PYTHON_DEPS_REAL=1 executes those generated recipes and uses the installed package offline.

tests.name: TestPythonDependenciesRejectInvalidUTF8
tests.says: Invalid UTF-8 anywhere in root or referenced requirements and constraints, including comments and after a BOM, is rejected before any Docker invocation without rewriting inputs.

tests.name: TestPythonDependenciesRejectBareCR
tests.says: Every CR not immediately followed by LF is rejected in root and referenced requirements and constraints before Docker, including comments, continuations and trailing bytes.

tests.name: TestPythonDependenciesRejectEncodingDeclarations
tests.says: Encoding declarations are rejected anywhere in every effective dependency file, even when declaring UTF-8, appearing beyond the first two lines or accompanying a BOM, before any Docker invocation.

tests.name: TestPythonDependenciesRejectEncodingDeclarationExploit
tests.says: The review's raw CR and unicode_escape declaration payload, hiding either --no-binary or --index-url, is rejected before Docker in root, referenced requirement and constraint files.

tests.name: TestPythonDependencyRecipeStagesTraversedDirectories
tests.says: Requirement and constraint references preserve every in-project directory they traverse, including empty directories canceled by '..', while retaining literal input bytes, canonical hashes and cache reuse; INVARIANT_PYTHON_DEPS_REAL=1 builds the generated recipes and verifies offline package execution.

tests.name: TestPythonDependenciesRejectUnsafeTraversal
tests.says: Every directory traversed by a requirement or constraint reference must stay inside the project and avoid symlinks, even when '..' cancels that directory and the final target is an existing in-project file; unsafe paths fail before Docker.

usage.summary: Revised [plan.json](/var/folders/fz/s3p17rl97r30y73d180fjbmc0000gn/T/invariant-plan-1466752743/plan.json) and acceptance tests, preserving prior scope and adding encoding and directory-traversal regressions. The checker passed: all 19 tests fail against the base code as required, and `repo/` remains unchanged.
